lorenz.title: A little chaos
lorenz.caption: A rotating view of the Lorenz attractor.
lorenz.description: A deterministic Lorenz system is integrated with small Euler steps, then projected into two dimensions. EasyCanvas supplies the coordinates and drawing loop; the attractor and projection are ordinary JavaScript. The changing colors show progress along the trajectory. This is a visual experiment, not a numerical solver for scientific use.

interference.title: Waves colliding
interference.caption: Move the pointer to move one wave source.
interference.description: Two radial sine waves overlap. At each grid cell, their amplitudes add and map to a color. Move your pointer across the plot to move one source. This uses the exposed canvas context for the colored cells and EasyCanvas inverse scales to convert their positions into data coordinates. Reduced-motion preferences freeze time while keeping pointer interaction.

sunflower.title: The golden-angle garden
sunflower.caption: Hundreds of dots. One surprisingly good angle.
sunflower.description: Each seed is placed at a radius proportional to the square root of its index, with successive angles separated by the golden angle. The resulting spiral pattern resembles phyllotaxis in plants. EasyCanvas scales place the seeds; native canvas arcs keep the dots round in pixel space. Move across the plot to nudge the angle and see the pattern reorganize.

spirograph.title: A pocket spirograph
spirograph.caption: Layered parametric loops, slowly breathing.
spirograph.description: A rolling-circle formula produces a hypotrochoid. Several colored versions of the curve are drawn with a small phase offset that changes over time. All coordinates are passed through EasyCanvas drawLine; there is no chart-specific helper or extra dependency. Reduced-motion preferences hold the phase still.
